name: No Parking
spec: white vertical rectangle with a black letter P inside a red circle with a red diagonal slash

snippets.back: Never park at NO PARKING signs, crosswalks, sidewalks, driveways, ramp three-foot zones, wheelchair curbs, disabled crosshatch, zero-emission bays, tunnels, bridges, hydrant and station fifteen-foot zones, crosswalk twenty-foot zones or fifteen at curb extensions, safety gaps, or doubled up.
Do not park in a posted No Parking, No Standing or No Stopping zone.
Regulatory examples in the manual include signs that ban right turns, left turns, U-turns or all turns, plus Left Turn Only, Do Not Enter, Wrong Way, No Parking, No Turn on Red and Do Not Pass.
Never park where no stopping, no standing or no parking signs are posted, or within five hundred feet of a fire or crash.

You also may not park beside a yellow-painted curb, where official No Parking signs stand, next to or opposite an excavation or obstacle if you would block traffic, or in front of mailboxes where local rules forbid it.
Colored curb markings can signal a parking limit even where no sign is posted, and a curb painted yellow means no parking there.
A No Parking sign prohibits parking at the signed location.

No parking is allowed on a sidewalk, in front of a driveway, inside an intersection, next to or opposite a highway construction zone, beside an already parked vehicle, on a bridge or in a tunnel, or in a bicycle lane unless your vehicle is disabled.
